name: Theodore Roosevelt
role: Rancher (Elkhorn, Maltese Cross); chairman of Little Missouri stockgrowers' association
bio: The future president, then a New York reformer and Bad Lands rancher, first appears in June 1884 visiting his ranch managed by Ferris & Merrifield and calling at the Cow Boy office in full cowboy dress. In December 1884 he called a meeting of Little Missouri stockmen and chaired it, and through 1886 the paper printed his notices as chairman and president of the Little Missouri River Stockmen's (later Stockgrowers') Association, whose meetings and round-ups he called. In May 1885 fifteen hundred yearlings and two-year-olds arrived for his Elkhorn and Chimney Butte ranches, and that year the paper noted his published account of a Big Horn hunt and an elk he shot down the river. In February 1886 it reported about 100 applications for jobs on his ranch after a lecture he gave on ranch life, and in April it praised his brisk handling of the stock meeting. That fall he and the Marquis de Morès guaranteed the money to kill and bury a quarantined, diseased herd, and in November he telegraphed the Ferris brothers that he had lost the election for mayor of New York.
